This post is a [marimo](https://marimo.io) notebook with its own layout, so it lives on its own page.

<img src="preview_image.png" alt="Two fitted sales models propagated through the same return initiation and receipt stages" style="width:100%; max-width:720px; border:1px solid #dcded1;">

**[Read the post &rarr;](returns-forecasting.html)**

Warehouse receipts depend on the returns customers start this week, which depend on what sold last month and what sells this month. The post starts with the [ttenet](https://github.com/kylejcaron/ttenet) API: a `RetailReturnModel` containing a NumPyro `CountProcess` and two `EventProcess` stages. It opens the underlying event models, then shows how one forecast call carries sales and weather uncertainty through the chain.

The sales step follows the ordinary [numpyro_forecast](https://github.com/juanitorduz/numpyro_forecast) protocol. The post fits a replacement drifting local-level sales model and propagates its forecast through the already fitted return stages. Fitting a replacement model and overriding future scenarios are separate operations: the return stages do not need to be refitted for either forecast scenario.

ttenet is a demo package: a reference implementation of the idea, meant to be read, run and adapted rather than a maintained library.

The figures on the page are interactive and run in your browser: follow one purchase through its two clocks, step through the fitted chain, and switch between storm scenarios (no storm, the storm as forecast, one that lingers). Every scenario is computed ahead of time, so nothing on the page needs a server.

The notebook behind the page is [`examples/retail_returns_blog.py`](https://github.com/kylejcaron/ttenet/blob/73d29319a070b6ab68cd5fa2d47cf33fc30ad205/examples/retail_returns_blog.py). Running it refits the model and recomputes every figure:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/kylejcaron/ttenet && cd ttenet
git checkout 73d29319a070b6ab68cd5fa2d47cf33fc30ad205
uv sync --all-extras
uv run marimo run examples/retail_returns_blog.py
```
